summary: iter384 verification: platform crons (event reminders D-1, subscribed calendar sync, opportunistic sync-stale, cron auth + idempotency) AND Calendar drag-to-reschedule (move preserves duration, resize extends end_date, invalid end<start rejected). Backend pytest 5/5 PASS. Frontend drag E2E PASS end-to-end via HTML5 DnD dispatch against September 2026 view (drag source Sept 8 chip + drop target Sept 15 cell both visible without scrolling at 1920x1080). Added data-testid='cal-cell-YYYY-MM-DD' to MonthGrid cells for testability (missing before). No ITER384 leftover events remain in DB.

detailed_results.backend_cron_idempotency: PASS - same run_id to /api/cron/calendar-sync returns duplicate=true on second call; db.cron_runs row keyed on {run_id, job}.
detailed_results.backend_event_reminders_once_per_holder: PASS - created paid event tomorrow with a booking, triggered cron, polled /api/public/bookings/status until reminder_sent_at populated; second run with a fresh run_id did NOT bump reminder_sent_at (no double-send).
detailed_results.backend_opportunistic_sync_stale_safe: PASS - POST /api/events/imported-calendars/sync-stale returns 200 with {refreshed, events, errors} shape even when nothing is stale.
detailed_results.backend_drag_move_and_resize_payloads: PASS - PUT /api/events/<id> accepts {date, end_date} shift (preserves duration), accepts isolated {end_date} extension, returns 400 'end date ...' when end_date < start.
detailed_results.frontend_drag_source_target_visibility: PASS - at 1920x1080 on September 2026 view: QA_DRAG_iter384 Sept 8 chip at y=353 (bottom 372) and Sept 15 target cell at y=415 (bottom 515) are both fully within the 1080 viewport without any scrolling.
detailed_results.frontend_move_drag: PASS - dispatched HTML5 dragstart/dragover/drop from cal-item-<id> to cal-cell-2026-09-15. Toast: '"QA_DRAG_iter384_5c8d" moved to 2026-09-15'. GET /api/events/<id> returned date=2026-09-15, end_date=2026-09-17 (duration = 2 extra days preserved).
detailed_results.frontend_resize_drag_extend: PASS - resize grip on last-day segment (cal-resize-<id>_d3) drag to cal-cell-2026-09-22 produced toast '"..." now runs to 2026-09-22'; backend end_date updated to 2026-09-22.
detailed_results.frontend_resize_rejects_end_before_start: PASS - dragging the resize grip to cal-cell-2026-09-01 (before current start 2026-09-15) surfaced the inline toast 'An event can't end before it starts' and the event remained date=2026-09-15, end_date=2026-09-22 (no backend write).

critical_code_review_comments: CalendarPage.jsx dropOnDate uses optimistic setRawEvents followed by eventsApi.update; on 409 it toasts 'Venue already booked' and loadAll(). Good surfacing.
cron.py _seen_before guard: dedupe key is {run_id, job} so the SAME run_id can be reused across different jobs - correct, and matches the test.

The resize handle is only rendered on the last day of a multi-day event (`!it._multiDay || it._spanEnd`) which is right, but its data-testid uses the per-day synthetic id (`cal-resize-<realId>_d{idx}`). That's not wrong, just something tests must account for (I did: scanned document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid^=cal-resize-<id>]') and took the last one).
startDrag reads `it._eventId || it.id` so dragging from a day-N copy correctly routes to the real event id - verified.

context_for_next_testing_agent: iter384 drag-to-reschedule works end-to-end. Playwright's native drag_to() does NOT fire the HTML5 DnD handlers against this React calendar - you MUST dispatch 'dragstart', 'dragenter', 'dragover', 'drop', 'dragend' manually with a shared DataTransfer via page.evaluate (see /app/test_reports/iteration_254.json detailed_results). cal-cell-YYYY-MM-DD testid now exists for Month view; Week/Day cells still lack one. The resize handle testid for multi-day events is cal-resize-<id>_d{spanLast}, not plain cal-resize-<id>.
